What happens before a drill reaches you?

A customer orders a cordless drill. Behind that purchase, components are sourced, the product is built and delivered, and suppliers are paid. Two connected processes make that happen.

Order to Delivery

Fulfils the customer’s order, from the order request to production and final delivery.

Starts with the customer order.Includes production and distribution.Ends when the customer receives the drill.
Procure to Pay

Obtains components from suppliers and completes the payment to those suppliers.

Begins with ordering the required parts.Includes receiving components and invoices.Ends when the supplier is paid.
Your task

Journey complete

Logistics moves the drill. Orchestration connects the journey.

Order to Delivery (OTD) and Procure to Pay (PTP) operate together. The customer sees an order and a parcel, but many coordinated activities make that experience possible.

Key takeaway: moving the product is only part of supply chain management. Information coordinates the network, material flows move goods through it, and financial flows sustain participation.

Information flow

Customer orders, component orders, receipts and invoices coordinate the work.

Material flow

Components reach the factory; the finished drill moves to the warehouse and customer.

Financial flow

The customer pays the retailer, and the manufacturer pays the supplier.
